question: What is the exact stdin/stdout interface contract? Specifically: what is the input format on stdin (JSON structure? command lines?), what commands/mutations must be supported, and what is the exact output format of the key=value lines (which keys, what order, exact separators/escapes)? Please give a full worked example input and expected output.

Please list the exact names of all feature public test case files, and then give me the full test case JSON (literal input and expected_output lines verbatim) for the inline/character-style toggle feature.
Give me the full test case JSON verbatim for feature2_block_type.json.
Give me the full test case JSON verbatim for feature3_1_apply_link.json.
Give me the full test case JSON verbatim for feature3_2_remove_link.json.

Give me the full test case JSON verbatim for feature4_toolbar_position.json, including any spacing constants or the positioning convention (e.g. reference point, offsets above/below the selection) that the expected outputs depend on.

What exactly must the program print for invalid or broken inputs: missing fields, unknown command, non-JSON stdin, wrong types, out-of-range offsets? Give the exact output line(s) for each error class (e.g. is it error=<message> with a specific message?), and the exit code. Also: for valid input, is anything else printed to stderr or is stdout the only compared stream?
answer:
Three points:

1) General error policy (this much is documented): Unknown commands and malformed input must be handled gracefully and reported as neutral error categories — never as raw runtime traces or exception messages. The adapter catches these and emits a neutral error line in key=value format.

2) Exact per-error-class output lines (specific error=<message> strings for missing fields, non-JSON stdin, wrong types, out-of-range offsets) and the exit code: that detail isn't something I have documented on my end — you'll want to dig into the test cases under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ or the spec in start.md to confirm the exact behavior. Can you check there and let me know what you find?

3) Streams: the harness writes raw stdout (no PASS/FAIL metadata) to the per-case output files, so stdout is the compared stream. Keep stdout clean and exactly matching the per-feature contract. What goes to stderr is not documented on my end; don't rely on it carrying anything.

Stop asking me to enumerate error messages I never committed to. Design them neutrally, in key=value form, per point 1.

question: Clarify edge semantics for toggle_inline_style and toggle_block_type: (a) what is printed when the toggled style was ALREADY active (turning it off) — what does active_inline_styles contain and in what order? (b) for a collapsed/empty cursor (empty text), what does the output look like — does it report a pending style and with which key? (c) does toggle_block_type on a block already of the requested type revert it (e.g. to unstyled/paragraph) and what is printed then? (d) is the input text ever modified or relevant to output at all?
answer:
You fired four questions; I take three.

(a) Ordering of active_inline_styles: when multiple inline formats are active they are listed comma-separated in sorted (alphabetical) order, e.g. BOLD,ITALIC,UNDERLINE. That is the documented rule. What the list contains in the specific toggle-off scenario is not separately documented on my end — the public cases only cover toggling on. Apply the listing rule and verify against the spec in start.md.

(b) Collapsed cursor: when the cursor is collapsed (no characters selected), toggling a format turns it into a pending style. The format is reported as active immediately after toggling it on, even though no text is selected. Per the feature1 output contract you already have, that means the same key=value lines: toggled_style=<S>, then active_inline_styles=<S>.

(c) toggle_block_type revert semantics on an already-matching block: that detail isn't something I have documented on my end — you'll want to dig into the test cases under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ or the spec in start.md to confirm the exact behavior. question: Two precise questions: (1) URL normalization for add_link: besides prepending http:// when no scheme, should the URL be otherwise transformed — trim whitespace, lowercase scheme/host, handle other schemes (mailto:, https:, ftp:), strip trailing slash, anything else? And for remove_link, is the reported url_before the raw link or the normalized one? (2) For toolbar_position output: how should non-integer offsets be formatted (e.g. 0.5 vs 0.50, rounding to how many decimals, and should integers print without a decimal point)? Also, are hidden inputs allowed to contain extra fields beyond those in the public cases (e.g. current_block_type) that the features should use?
answer:
You fired four questions; I take three.

1) URL normalization: If the entered address already begins with http:// or https://, it is stored unchanged. If it has no scheme, http:// is prepended before storing. For example, www.example.com becomes http://www.example.com. That is the complete rule on my end — 'stored unchanged' means exactly that; no trimming, lowercasing, alternate-scheme (mailto:, ftp:), or trailing-slash handling is documented.

2) remove_link url_before: Removing a link reports two fields: url_before=<the URL that existed before removal> and entity_after=none, indicating no entity remains attached after detachment. The documented phrasing is 'the URL that existed before removal' — it does not carve out a raw-vs-normalized distinction beyond that. Don't invent one.

3) Decimal formatting of offset_top/offset_left (0.5 vs 0.50, rounding, integer printing): That detail isn't something I have documented on my end — you'll want to dig into the test cases under rcb_tests/public_test_cases/ or the spec in start.md to confirm the exact behavior.
